name: Tawang Monastery (Galden Namgyal Lhatse)
description: Largest Buddhist monastery in India and second-largest in the world, founded in 1680-81 by Merak Lama Lodre Gyatso. Houses a 28-foot gilded Buddha statue, ancient manuscripts, and is the spiritual heart of the Monpa community. Birthplace region of the 6th Dalai Lama; overlooks the Tawang Chu valley.
facts: Founded 1680-81 following wishes of 5th Dalai Lama
Famous for Torgya and Losar festivals

name: Bomdila
description: Headquarters of West Kameng district, a hill station at about 2,415 m offering panoramic Himalayan views, apple orchards, and Buddhist monasteries. Gateway on the route to Tawang with markets, lodges, and cool climate.
facts: Known for Rhododendron Festival in April

name: Bomdila Monastery (Gontse Gaden Rabgyel Ling / GRL)
description: Important Gelug monastery complex in Bomdila with Upper and Lower Gompas, established in 1965 and consecrated by the Dalai Lama. Features Tibetan-style architecture, prayer halls, and a monastic school overlooking the town.
facts: Upper Gompa on hilltop with school
Popular spiritual stop on Tawang route

name: Dirang
description: Scenic valley town in West Kameng at about 1,620 m, known for its river, orchards, hot springs, and monasteries. Base for exploring Sangti Valley, Mandala Top, and Thembang; site of a geothermal energy project.
facts: On NH-13 between Bomdila and Tawang
Home to National Institute of Mountaineering

name: Sangti Valley
description: Picturesque valley about 14 km from Dirang, surrounded by Himalayan ranges, with meadows, river, orchards, and winter visits by black-necked cranes. Ideal for picnics, birdwatching, and quiet stays at sheep farms or homestays.

name: Thembang Fortified Village
description: Ancient Monpa fortified village with traditional Dzong, stone gates, wood carvings, and manuscripts. UNESCO tentative World Heritage site representing living heritage of the region; located about 55 km northeast of Bomdila.
facts: Ancient fortified settlement with northern and southern gates

name: Eaglenest Wildlife Sanctuary
description: Biodiversity hotspot sanctuary in West Kameng spanning 500-3,250 m elevation, famous for bird diversity including the endemic Bugun Liocichla. Conjoins Sessa Orchid Sanctuary; part of Kameng Elephant Reserve with dense forests and high ridges.
facts: Important for rare pheasants and mammals

name: Sessa Orchid Sanctuary
description: Protected area dedicated to orchid conservation in West Kameng, covering about 100 km² with over 200 orchid species. Conjoins Eaglenest; features research centre nearby at Tippi and trekking routes through varied habitats.
facts: Part of Kameng Protected Area Complex
Supported by Tippi Orchid Research Centre

name: Tippi Orchid Research Centre
description: Research and cultivation centre near Tippi/Bhalukpong showcasing thousands of orchid species in glass houses. Gateway attraction on the Assam-Arunachal route with species house, herbarium, and tissue culture facilities.

name: Nyukmadong War Memorial
description: Memorial in the form of a 25-foot chorten commemorating the Battle of Nyukmadong on 18 November 1962, where Indian forces under Brigadier Hoshiar Singh fought advancing Chinese troops. Located on the highway between Dirang and Sela Pass.
facts: On NH-13 between Dirang and Sela

name: Bhalukpong
description: Gateway town at the foothills in southern West Kameng on the Kameng River, entry point from Assam with ILP check post. Base for river activities like angling and rafting; near Tippi Orchid Centre and Pakke border.
